title: OneDrive: convert a Copilot response into a Word file on the web
summary: The briefing passes: its planned behaviour and overdue target match the roadmap, and Microsoft documents the licensing and licence-assignment controls it gives. The searches found no conversion-only switch or documentation resolving this option's storage and label-inheritance details.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this specific OneDrive response-to-Word conversion feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "OneDrive" "convert" "response" "Word"; OneDrive Copilot convert response Word document admin switch pricing saved sensitivity label. Read previous-year-release-notes and OneDrive Get started/FAQ; results described other conversions and agents.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot has been renamed Microsoft Copilot, the name now used by the cited requirements and licensing pages.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot is now named Microsoft Copilot, and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is now named Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap nor the documentation found specifies where this converted Word file is saved or its resulting sharing arrangement.
claims.quote: Searched: "OneDrive" "response" "Word" "saved" "label"; "OneDrive" "convert" "response" "Word". Read roadmap, OneDrive FAQ/Get started, architecture-data-protection-auditing; storage results concerned Word agents, MCP tools or file pickers, not this option.

claims.where: What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap and documentation found do not specify the converted Word file's name.
claims.quote: Searched: "OneDrive" "response" "Word" "saved" "label"; "OneDrive" "convert" "response" "Word". Read roadmap and OneDrive Get started/FAQ; autogenerated names appeared for Copilot Studio Word MCP tools, not this conversion.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Whether this OneDrive conversion inherits sensitivity labels from the response's source files is not documented.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity

claims.quote: Now, with one click, you can convert any Copilot response into a Word document. This feature requires a Microsoft Copilot for Microsoft 365 license and will be available to commercial customers on OneDrive Web.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: No tenant-wide UI or automation switch specific to converting OneDrive Copilot responses into Word files is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive convert Copilot response Word SharePoint PowerShell Set-SPOTenant Microsoft Graph export switch; "OneDrive" "convert" "Copilot" "disable"; "Copilot" "OneDrive" "conversion" "admin". Read OneDrive FAQ and configure-copilot-admin-center; no conversion-only setting.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The conversion is user-opt-in: an available capability that each licensed user chooses to use.
claims.quote: Now, with one click, you can convert any Copilot response into a Word document. Searched: OneDrive convert Copilot response Word SharePoint PowerShell Set-SPOTenant Microsoft Graph export switch; read OneDrive FAQ and configure-copilot-admin-center; no feature-specific enablement switch.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions.
claims.quote: Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions. If content is already overshared, Copilot can surface it to anyone who has access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A DLP policy for Copilot can keep Copilot from summarising labelled files and emails.
claims.quote: A DLP policy for Copilot can keep Copilot from summarizing labeled files and emails. Copilot can still return a link so the user can open the item outside Copilot.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope: Admin roles; Governance controls
claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; rendered controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The licence-assignment control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.where: controls[1].api; rendered controls table
claims.claim: Microsoft Graph PowerShell assigns a licence with Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @().
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Licence assignment governs licensed Microsoft Copilot capabilities generally, not this conversion option alone.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot license | Required for licensed Microsoft Copilot capabilities

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators can disable the Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint service plan, disabling Copilot in both OneDrive and SharePoint.
claims.quote: Copilot in OneDrive can be disabled in your service plan by your administrator by unchecking Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint from the Microsoft 365 admin center > Turn apps and services on or off. Note that this will disable Copilot in both OneDrive and SharePoint.
